newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soldiers kill nine guerrillas in Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: Indian soldiers kill nine guerrillas in Kashmir.

text.p: Indian soldiers killed nine guerrillas who had crossed the border from Pakistan into Kashmir, a defence spokesman said on Wednesday.
The militants were killed overnight in a gun battle Michil near the India-Pakistan border and about 85 km (55 miles) north of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state.
It was the third clash in the heavily wooded region this month. Three separatist guerrillas and two paramilitary troopers were killed on Monday in the thick forests of Michil.
The defence spokesman said troops launched a large operation to flush out militants after Monday's clash.

"The militants in the besieged forest opened fire which resulted in a fierce encounter," he said. "Nine bodies of militants, most of them foreigners, were recovered last evening." He did not clarify the nationalities of those killed.
A large quantity of arms and ammunition was recovered, the spokesman said. "The search operation for recovery of arms and bodies is still going on," the spokesman said.
On June 7, Indian security forces shot dead 13 separatist guerrillas in the same area.
India accuses Pakistan of arming and training militants fighting New Delhi's rule in the Himalayan region. Islamabad says it provides only moral and diplomatic support.
Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died since a separatist revolt broke out in mostly Hindu India's only Moslem majority state in 1990.
